gaps.name: A move with no symlink lets delete retention remove sessions whose files are still on disk
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - an up-to-date pass never refreshes session_meta.transcript_path. After .claude moves with no symlink left behind, that column names a path that is gone, so retention's delete rule removes a session whose transcript is still on disk under the new root, along with its observation row, and the next pass archives the file a second time from offset 0.
gaps.evidence: crates/terminus-core/src/ingest/mod.rs:515-517: apply returns Outcome::UpToDate before the session_meta upsert at :1390-1397, which is the only place ingest writes transcript_path. crates/terminus-core/src/retention/mod.rs:206 and :248-253: the delete rule asks transcript_is_gone of that stored path. CONTEXT.md D-13 says ingest 'already overwrites [transcript_path] on every pass', which is false for an unchanged file. PLAN-2.md Task 3 (line 89) names this exact hazard, 'an old root's path would read as gone after a move made without a symlink', and fixes it only for merged twins. Probe on temp dirs: run 1 archived one session (8 turns). I then moved the root (mv a b, no symlink), set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=b and [retention] action = "delete", age_days = 30. Run 2 had files_seen 1 and committed 0, and its notes read 'retention deleted 1 session(s), removing 1 observation row(s) with them - the session's archive went too, so no rebuild reproduces them', while b/projects/-tmp-p/11111111-...jsonl (5,656 bytes) was still on disk. Run 3 archived it again from offset 0 with 8 turns added. On a real store the new session_no would differ, leaving label and decision turn ids naming nothing. Not a regression: before this phase the same move archived new copies under new keys and retention deleted the old ones, losing the same rows.
gaps.missing: Make the stored transcript_path follow the file. When a walk reads a session's file at a path other than session_meta.transcript_path, rewrite the column even when the pass is up to date. The alternative is for retention to decide 'gone' from the session's key against what discovery yields, not from the stored path. Add a regression test: archive a session, move the root with no symlink, enable delete retention past the session's age, run a pass, and assert the session and its observation row are still there with the same session_no.
